result.title: Predictable Scaling: Efficient Model Exploration via Scaling-Law Prediction
result.summary: Evaluating candidate changes (hypotheses) to recommendation models requires full-scale training runs consuming thousands of GPU-hours, severely limiting the hypothesis space engineers can feasibly explore. We introduce Predictable Scaling (PS), a systematic framework that exploits empirically verified regularity conditions to predict full-scale model performance from small-scale proxies. PS constructs scaled-down variants via composable scaling functions along distinct resource axes, and projects metrics to the target scale via curve fitting with calibrated uncertainty estimates. We compare three prediction strategies of increasing expressiveness: even the simplest (raw proxy) achieves prediction error within the empirical noise floor of repeated-run variance; the most expressive (Gaussian Process) provides an indicative 15% relative MAE improvement and calibrated uncertainty. Evaluation on two ranking models of increasing complexity---a task-specific model and a foundation model---demonstrates that PS correctly ranks actionable hypotheses across diverse hypothesis types at 79-88% compute reductions.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Predictable Scaling 框架：沿不同资源轴用可组合缩放函数构造小规模代理模型，通过曲线拟合和不确定性校准，从低成本小规模实验预测推荐/排序模型的全规模性能，并在两个排序模型上实现假设排序与 79–88% 的算力削减。
AI.relevance_reason: 与视觉推理主线无直接关联，但其「小规模代理预测全规模性能」及不确定性校准的思路，可能可供核查用于低成本估计 LVR 中 THINK 长度或计算预算的收益与成本，需确认其缩放规律是否适用于多模态推理状态。
